question: Chapter 1.6 of the Handbook on Victims of Terrorism sets out a detailed list of examples of secondary victimisation of victims of terrorism, but they do not include humiliation and attacks on the image of victims or glorifying a specific crime or paying tribute to convicted offenders. The Commission has been repeatedly asked to update the Handbook and to add these cases to the list.

The Commission’s response has been evasive, since it has never assessed the proposal, but also contradictory, in replying that the aim of the Handbook is to present in a comprehensive manner the causes of secondary victimisation of victims, without being particularly explicit, although the Handbook in fact gives seven explicit examples. I would therefore like to ask the Commission again: 1.

Does it plan to update the EU Handbook on Victims of Terrorism in the near future and to include humiliation and attacks on the image of victims, as well as glorification of a specific crime or paying tribute to convicted offenders, as examples of secondary victimisation?
Could a failure to include such an update lead to a lack of protection of, and even discrimination against, victims of terrorism who suffer the negative effects of such acts?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.5.2024) In view of the increased threats to security in the EU that terrorism presents, the Commission is committed to ensuring that victims of terrorism can rely on their rights independently of where in the EU a terrorist attack takes place.

The EU adopted a solid set of rules on victims’ rights, including particular provisions on rights of victims of terrorism that meet more directly their specific needs, as well as the right to protection from secondary and repeat victimisation.

In order to facilitate the practical application of the EU rules on the rights of victims of terrorism, the Commission has ensured the functioning of the EU Centre of Expertise for Victims of Terrorism and has published the EU Handbook on Victims of Terrorism (the EU Handbook)1.

The latter sets out a non-exhaustive list of examples of secondary victimisation of victims of terrorism, which do not currently include humiliation and attacks on the image of victims or glorifying a specific crime or paying tribute to convicted offenders.

The Commission has carefully considered the suggestion to include these cases in the EU Handbook and complementing it, in order to clarify certain aspects presented in it, such as protection of victims of terrorism from secondary victimisation.

In this context, humiliation and attacks on the image of victims, as well as glorification of a specific crime or paying tribute to convicted offenders, could be incorporated as examples of secondary victimisation.

This is to be seen in combination with the Radicalisation Awareness Network ‘Practitioners’, which addressed the subject of the image of victims of terrorism in the media, including restraint from glorifying terrorist acts2.
1 The EU Centre offers a platform for national authorities and victim support organisations in Member States to

exchange knowledge and experience on rights of victims of terrorism. For reference: https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/policies/justice-and-fundamental-rights/criminaljustice/protecting-victims-rights/eu-centre-expertise-victims-terrorism_en 2 Reporting about Violent Extremism and P/CVE Challenges for Journalists – Recommendations from Practitioners, https://home-affairs.ec.europa.
